_comment: The host-component manifest (PRD §5.2.12). This file IS the §15.4 version
matrix — there is no second copy to drift from it.
Every hash here is compiled into the binary by go:embed and is the only
authority on what an artefact must contain. Hashes are never fetched: one
downloaded from beside the artefact proves only that the two agree. The
consequence is deliberate — bumping a component is a change to this file,
which goes through review and the §14 gates.
Versions are the ones M0 validated. Changing one means re-running the
relevant spike, not editing a number: spikes/cilium-standalone found the
writable service REST API removed in Cilium 1.18, and spikes/kaniko-build
found BuildKit's frontend defaulting to Dockerfile. Both are the kind of
thing a patch bump can reintroduce.

components.name: cni-plugins
components._files: The whole archive is extracted into the CNI bin directory: the plugin set is what the conflist may reference, and picking a subset here means a conflist edit becomes a manifest edit.

components.name: etcd
components.summary: Cilium kvstore (derived state, never backed up)

components.name: cilium
components.summary: eBPF dataplane; runs as a containerd task
components._digest: The multi-arch index digest, so one pin covers both architectures and containerd resolves the per-arch manifest itself.
components._files: Only these two. cilium-agent stays inside the image and runs as a task — it needs its bundled helpers, iptables and BPF templates, and unpacking that onto a host is unsupported upstream (PRD §5.2.12). cilium-cni has to be a host file because containerd execs it.

components.name: buildkit
components.summary: rootless build daemon (the only build driver)
components._files: Unlike cilium, these extract cleanly and run on the host — PRD §23.2 already specified it that way.
